_note: MS02: Z1 apply of the C campaign (C1 adhoc DMA order, C2 NMITIMEN callers, C3 boot / reset / MEMSEL, C4 displayModeFlags). Union of specs/C1_notes.json (only the two entries C2 does not replace: radar_map_screen comment 229608 and system_core comment 33215), specs/C2_notes.json (replaces the C1 drafts for the hdma_dma_spc block note and the AdhocVramDma part note), specs/C3_notes.json and specs/C4_notes.json. Dry-run first: npm run merge -- plans/extracted-audit/edits/MS02.json --dry-run. Comments go through expectOld because extracted/ carries no line-tracking tags. 'find' must occur exactly once in the stored note.

edit.find: Writers must store the size before the destination (the destination arms the transfer).
edit.with: The destination word is the pending flag: the NMI runs the transfer when it is nonzero. Both writers (RadarScreenSetup and the AdhocVramDma COP handler) store the destination before the size. Measured: in every pair (radar screen, credits scene, boot) the NMI was off at both stores and no NMI ran between them. Actors normally run with NMITIMEN = $01, but the first UpdateFrameDialogue pass after a scene load runs RunActors_CutsceneOnly with NMITIMEN = $81, and neither writer guards against an NMI between its two stores there. A writer that can run with the NMI on has to store the size first.

229608.text: Destination word = pending flag for the next NMI; the NMI is off here (NMITIMEN = $01), so it cannot run before the size store below
229608.expectOld: Writing the destination arms the adhoc DMA; the size is stored after it (writers should store the size first)

edit.find: The destination word is written before the size word, but the NMI fires on a nonzero destination.
edit.with: The destination word is written before the size word, and the NMI runs the transfer when the destination is nonzero. Actors normally execute with NMITIMEN = $01 (NMI off), so no NMI can run between the two stores; UpdateFrameFull switches the NMI off first. The first UpdateFrameDialogue pass after a scene load runs actors with NMITIMEN = $81 and has no such protection.

edit.find: 3. MEMSEL = 1 (but InitHardwareRegisters writes MEMSEL = 0 afterwards: boot stays SlowROM until sFB_boot_logo enables FastROM)
edit.with: 3. MEMSEL = 1: FastROM timing lasts only for the register-init loop of InitHardwareRegisters, whose last table entry writes MEMSEL = 0. The WRAM clear, the SPC engine upload (video frames 3 to 7 after reset) and the first scene loads run with SlowROM timing until BootLogoInit (frame 84) writes MEMSEL = 1. Measured: the upload takes the same number of master clocks with FastROM timing, because it waits on the SPC port handshake

edit.find: No writer of $83 at $0100 was found (dialog_string_scanner uses $0100 as scratch).
edit.with: No writer of $83 at $0100 was found (dialog_string_scanner uses $0100 as scratch). InitSystemVariables skips the stack page, so after a cold boot the byte holds power-on RAM contents and after a reset the value the game left there. Measured with the byte at $83, $00, $5A and random power-on values: the branch is taken only for $83 and skips the second LDY; the first sceneNext write (0), the frame of every later boot step and the scene sequence are identical

32807.text: MEMSEL = 1: FastROM timing only for the register-init loop; its last table entry writes 0, so the boot stays SlowROM until BootLogoInit
32807.expectOld: MEMSEL = 1; InitHardwareRegisters writes 0 again below, so boot stays SlowROM until sFB_boot_logo

229449.expectOld: Restore NMI-only mode (disable joypad auto-read during inventory teardown)

229519.expectOld: Display loop: enable NMI+joypad, wait for VBlank (joypad is read), back to NMI-only

edit.find: and a chain of VBlank sync/NMI enable calls.
edit.with: and a chain of VBlank sync/NMI enable calls. The last call of the chain, EnableNmiAndJoypad, leaves NMITIMEN = $81 into the enter transition: the first UpdateFrameDialogue pass runs RunActors_CutsceneOnly with the NMI on, and the DisableNmiKeepJoypad at the end of that pass turns it off.

use the same flag. A reset clears it too: the boot WRAM clear (InitSystemVariables) zeroes $0A02, so every boot starts with the first logo. Measured after a reset with the flag set at the title and after a reset with the flag set by the game during the second logo: the first logo plays in both cases.

edit.find: if set, the upload is suppressed (returns immediately).
edit.with: if set, the upload is suppressed (returns immediately): the request bits stay pending and the upload runs in the first NMI after the bit is cleared (measured). No instruction sets this bit; the PAUSE path of GlobalInputHandler clears it.

edit.find: the common TRB below clears bits 0, 4 and 5 either way.
edit.with: the common TRB below clears bits 0, 4 and 5 either way. Measured: bit 0 gives the full upload and bit 4 or bit 5 gives the same partial upload (VRAM words $7840-$7983 = staging offsets $80-$1BF), each in the first NMI after the request, which also clears the bit. The ROM only ever requests bit 4 (UpdateHUD, three sites); no instruction sets bit 5.
